article.headline: Changing the order of diffusion as video noise falls
article.lead: S2PD applies autoregressive diffusion at high noise and switches to parallel diffusion at low noise. The division suggests a concrete experiment: vary the switch point and see which events remain physically and logically consistent.

picks.question: How sensitive are event order and physical consistency to the noise level at which generation switches to parallel updates?

paragraphs.text: S2PD establishes temporal structure serially while the video is noisy, then denoises frames in parallel. Two other papers address longer rollouts. ID-Forcing examines the provenance of cached keys and values at test time. HLA-WM uses hybrid linear attention to manage the memory cost of maintaining scene consistency.

ChronoWorld conditions 4D generation on camera control, spatiotemporal cues and geometric feedback. MC-Sparse looks inside diffusion transformers and selects individual key-value tokens for attention. These papers give different diagnostic views of a failing clip: the geometry under camera motion and the information a frame can still attend to.

sections.heading: Testing what a world model knows about actions

paragraphs.text: TAPDreamer uses a public encoder to construct transferable adversarial patches for world-action models without querying the target policy. H-JEPA studies planning at multiple timescales in an action-conditioned visual representation. A separate textual world-modeling paper tracks structured descriptions of state to limit error accumulation across a rollout.

AffordCraft retrieves parts to build task-ready simulation assets from a single RGB image. DeskForge constructs annotated desktop scenes for computer-use supervision. Video2Skill asks whether a vision-language model can extract a reusable manipulation skill from streaming experience. Each changes the training or evaluation material a policy can learn from.

UniSlider remaps a generative editor's strength control so equal slider movements produce more uniform perceptual changes. DEPICT evaluates prompt-image agreement through answers to questions, including cases where a prompt explicitly excludes an object.

The Empirical Variational Autoencoder learns an autoregressive latent prior for continuous sequences. GeoSET uses paired synthetic-aperture radar and optical images to learn translation between sensors. OmniReasoningBench adds 1,150 questions designed to require joint use of sound and vision.

DeepGEMM provides GPU matrix-multiplication kernels. Rapid-MLX serves language models on Apple Silicon and reports speed improvements relative to mlx-lm with matching weights. For reproduction, identify the exact hardware and decoding workload in each repository.

Two model announcements also entered the archive: Reflection's 501B open-weight Beam and Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk. Their release pages are the place to check supported modalities, memory requirements and evaluation settings before choosing a deployment target.
